Apply the gradient formula $m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$ for points $A$ and $B$:
$$m_{AB} = \frac{(3k + 5) - (k + 3)}{(k + 3) - (-3k - 1)} = \frac{2k + 2}{4k + 4}$$

Factorise and simplify the fraction (valid since $k \ne -1$):
$$m_{AB} = \frac{2(k + 1)}{4(k + 1)} = \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$$
$$\text{Since } m_{AB} = \frac{1}{2} \text{ contains no } k, \text{ the gradient is independent of } k$$

Calculate the midpoint $M$ of the line segment $AB$ in terms of $k$:
$$M = \left( \frac{-3k - 1 + k + 3}{2}, \, \frac{k + 3 + 3k + 5}{2} \right) = \left( \frac{-2k + 2}{2}, \, \frac{4k + 8}{2} \right) = (1 - k, \, 2k + 4)$$

Determine the gradient of the perpendicular bisector:
$$m_\perp = -\frac{1}{m_{AB}} = -\frac{1}{1/2} = -2$$

Form and simplify the equation of the line passing through $M$:
$$y - (2k + 4) = -2\left[ x - (1 - k) \right]$$
$$y - 2k - 4 = -2x + 2(1 - k) = -2x + 2 - 2k$$
$$y + 2x = 6 \quad (\text{or } y = -2x + 6)$$
